newsitem.title: USA: U.S. governors applaud budget deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. governors applaud budget deal.

text.p: State governors attending their annual meeting Tuesday hailed the budget agreement between President Clinton and House Republicans, especially provisions to extend health care to poor children.

"In charting a new course toward expanding (medical insurance) coverage to more uninsured children, Congress and the president are giving states the ability to build on their successes in designing health insurance programmes that meet the unique needs of their states," they said in a joint statement.

The 50 governors "applauded the president and Congress for giving states the opportunity to continue their success in extending health insurance to more uninsured children -- a reality made possible by provisions in the budget accord anounced today on Capitol Hill," they said.

"Governors have made significant progress in extending coverage to uninsured children," said the National Governors' Conference chairman Gov. Bob Miller of Nevada and vice chairman, Ohio's George Voinovich.

"With state flexibility to design more meaningful and comprehensive benefits packages, coverage numbers will increase substantially. States have already demonstrated important progress in covering more children with innovative plans that expand health coverage to uninsured children, including several expansion programmes funded entirely with state money or through public-private partnerships," they said.

The governors, meeting in Las Vegas for their annual conference, noted that 40 states have expanded Medicaid coverage beyond federally mandated levels and said the governors were looking forward to working with Congress and the White House to expand health care access to even more children.
